hypothesis.statement: The ranking rule is now NAMED, and it is not declaration order. Across the two states measured on this function, MWCC ranks the callee-saved bank as: (1) memory-LOADED locals, in declaration order; (2) a local that is a COPY OF A PARAMETER; (3) parameters used directly. The committed state has five locals and gives r31 to the arrH[].d load (`@0x58 lwz r31,548(r3)`) and r30 to the node copy (`@0x24 addi r30,r7,0`), i.e. the loaded local outranks the copy local; the probe state has four locals plus a directly-used parameter and gives r31 to the same load, r30/r29/r28 to the three remaining loaded/computed locals in declaration order (`@0x50 lwz r30,536(r3)`, `@0x60 add r29,r6,r0`, `@0x5c lwz r28,552(r3)`) and r27 - the BOTTOM of the bank - to the parameter (`@0x24 addi r27,r7,0`); the `m` parameter's copy sits at `@0x20 addi r26,r5,0` in BOTH streams, below everything, which is the same rule seen a third time. The target inverts only the top pair, so in the retail source the node value must have been in class (1) or ahead of the arrH[].d load, and no spelling of a parameter copy reaches class (1). The remaining direction is therefore to demote the OTHER value out of class (1): find a form in which `d` is not a memory load that survives the two calls - for example loading it from the config block AFTER `DrawNormalText` returns, so it never needs a callee-saved home at all, or reading it through a pointer whose own web is already callee-saved. That must be done without moving the `lwz` at 0x58, which is the constraint every previous probe broke. If that also fails, this function is source-exhausted at 8 differing words, MNEMONIC DIVERGENCE 0, CLASS RECOLOR, and it is a clean, provenanced customer for the shipped copy_register_fields + verify_consistent_recolor composition.
